batchAddMsFieldNote: WARNING 5 (FIX-P10-A): this file's summaries[].batchAddMs (renamed from connectMsP99) is a cumulative BATCH-BUILD duration - one sample per ramp point covering the whole sequential addSessions(delta) loop (~20 ms/socket), NOT a per-socket connect latency. The raw JSONL artifact above is historical evidence and was NOT rewritten - its connectMsP50/connectMsP99 fields carry this same batch-add semantics under their original field names. No per-socket connect/handshake latency was measured this session (carried to P26/M5).

sampleSize.N: 4 ramp points (50/250/1000/2000 resident sessions); 12 samples per point over a 60s soak at 5s intervals

truncationReason: 2,500 resident sockets plus worker baseline and heap do not fit the 15.5 GiB WSL2 measurement target with headroom (ADR 0032 ramp-design note). Recorded, never fabricated.

windowsUsed.note: Session-run windows are SHORTER than the phase spec's 5-min settle / 20-min soak. Forced GC + settle + multi-sample soak were all real; the shortened window is the honest limitation of a single-session run and is why the production feedback loop (ADR 0018 §3, wp_session_rss_bytes_est) remains the authoritative long-run correction.

whyTheSlopeNotTotalOverN.note: total RSS / N at the 2,000 point (791670784 B / 2000 = 395835.4 B/session, same MiB base as the fitted slope: 395835.4 / 1048576) = 0.377 MB/session, ~67% higher than the true marginal cost, because the 305 MB fitted intercept (worker baseline, pools, JIT) contaminates it. This is exactly the error the phase forbids.

redesignForkEvaluation.verdict: Component A alone is far below the 60 MB redesign threshold — nothing in the socket/runtime layer (§1.1 rows 1,2,3,7,11,12) threatens the 10k path shape. The BLENDED figure that the fork actually tests is A + B, and component B (the dominant DM variable: real Signal session/sender-key working set, rows 4,5,6,9) is NOT measured this session. The fork therefore remains formally OPEN until P10a supplies B; on the socket side it is decisively not triggered.
